# NOTICE Template

Fill in the blanks (`<...>`). Delete buckets the repo does not use. Keep the order: project identity, license summary, fork lineage (conditional), third-party reference material (conditional), carve-outs, authoritativeness statement.

The emitted `NOTICE` file has no leading `#` heading and no extensionless-file SPDX header — it is covered by the `REUSE.toml` prose-group annotation.

## Template body

```text
<Project Name>

Copyright <year(s)> <author or organization>

This repository contains material under multiple licenses.

Project-authored substantive source code is licensed as follows:
  - Lean code (`**/*.lean`) under the Apache License 2.0. See
    LICENSES/Apache-2.0.txt.
  - Other substantive code (Python scripts, shell tools, shared LaTeX
    macros and filters) under the MIT License. See LICENSES/MIT.txt.

Hand-authored infrastructure config — Makefiles, lakefile.toml,
pyproject.toml, YAML, JSONC, .editorconfig, .gitignore, word lists,
and similar — is licensed under MIT via the `REUSE.toml` config-group
annotation. These files are not content the project asserts substantive
authorship over; the REUSE.toml glob keeps lint clean without per-file
sidecars or inline headers on every dotfile.

Project-authored prose — framework documents, explainers, planning
notes, paper manuscripts, READMEs, and this NOTICE — is licensed under
Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0). See
LICENSES/CC-BY-4.0.txt. This material is covered by the `REUSE.toml`
prose-group annotation; per-file SPDX headers are not required for
prose.

<Optional: include only if the repo has tracked generated artifacts
(lock files, Pandoc output, tool-regenerated JSON/ICS).>
Files auto-regenerated by tooling — lock files (uv.lock,
lake-manifest.json, package-lock.json), pinned-version files
(lean-toolchain), Pandoc-generated LaTeX, tool-produced JSON/JSONL/ICS
— are dedicated to the public domain under CC0 1.0. See
LICENSES/CC0-1.0.txt. Content is mechanical output the project does
not originate; the CC0 dedication is covered via the `REUSE.toml`
generated-group annotation rather than per-file headers.

<Optional: include only if CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md exists and is
Contributor-Covenant-derived.>
The CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md file is adapted from the Contributor Covenant
and is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0
International (CC BY-SA 4.0). See LICENSES/CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt.

<Optional: include only if the repo is a fork.>
This repository is a fork of <upstream URL>. Files retained from the
upstream tree keep their original copyright (<upstream copyright
line>) and original license (<upstream SPDX>). See the upstream
project for its authorship record. Fork-specific changes are
copyright <year(s)> <fork author>.

<Optional: include only if the repo bundles third-party reference
material.>
Third-party bundled reference materials are included for study,
verification, and scholarly context. They are covered under
LicenseRef-Reference-Material (see
LICENSES/LicenseRef-Reference-Material.txt). Paths covered:
  - references/papers/**     (source PDFs)
  - references/extractions/** (faithful OCR and transcription caches)
  - references/transcriptions/** (verbatim transcriptions of
                                  theorem statements and excerpts)
Copyright in those materials remains with the original authors and
publishers, as identified in the materials themselves. No license to
modify, redistribute, or republish is granted by this repository.

<Optional: per-work exception example; delete if not applicable.>
A narrower LicenseRef applies to <specific work> because <specific
rationale: e.g. the work has unusual prominence as the primary source
this repository formalizes>. See
LICENSES/LicenseRef-<Work-Specific>.txt.

The following paths fall outside the authored-license sweep and are
not covered by SPDX tags in this repository:
  - LICENSES/ itself (tool convention)
  - Vendored dependency state (e.g. proofs/.lake/packages/**,
    .venv/, node_modules/, .git/)
  - External shared corpora accessed via symlink (e.g. corpora/
    when it points outside the worktree)
  - Build artifacts and caches that are gitignored

Per-file SPDX metadata together with the root REUSE.toml prose-group
annotation is authoritative for this repository. This NOTICE is a
summary; it does not override per-file tags. See
https://reuse.software/ for the REUSE specification and tooling.
```

## Notes

- Use literal path globs in the template body (`references/papers/**`) rather than prose paraphrases — they double as a map of what is actually covered.
- Keep the final paragraph. It is the anti-override statement: any reader who skims `NOTICE` and assumes everything in the repo is under one license needs to be redirected to per-file tags.
- When updating an existing `NOTICE` rather than authoring fresh, preserve any incident-specific or legal-review-specific language that the user has added. The template is a starting point, not a stencil.
